verdict.rationale: Ghostty documents a single configuration system used by both its macOS and Linux apps (e.g., runtime config reload on each, Homebrew and Linux distro packages), and community users describe it as an option for macOS and Linux. There is no evidence of a Windows terminal app; only the libghostty-vt library is listed as Windows-compatible, and a developer building block earns no credit here. Docs also note that default keybindings differ per platform. Missing for 10: a Windows build of the Ghostty terminal itself, explicit documentation that one config file is portable across platforms, independent corroboration of shared configs across operating systems.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the same terminal with the same config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: The configuration can be reloaded at runtime by pressing `ctrl+shift+,` (Linux) or `cmd+shift+,` (macOS).
Ghostty is available in the default repositories for many Linux distributions.
it's great to have another modern high performance terminal as an option for macOS and Linux.
